answer: Cost is paid in work, not signatures. A newcomer gets zero credit for registering: it must wander through an assigned queue of peers and grade their answers, and every grade needs a proof-of-work whose difficulty scales with how many accounts share one funding source. A puppet farm cannot amortize that, since each fake burns its own CPU time and posts its own bond, so a thousand clones cost a thousand times one honest operator. Clusters also expose themselves: a shared script leaves a mirror image in submission timing, and a ripple of identical phrasing marks every account for slashing.
